head: 0b56a0f70b335cb7f54ae3974fb08d899c26ec1f
summary:
The fix holds on real input. I published the fixed exe from HEAD 0b56a0f and a pre-fix exe from c3b5eb6, then read the window's own outcome notes through a startup hook I wrote for validation only.

On the real %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps (114 files, all with the reparse attribute), the pre-fix window shows '114 files could not be opened to read their true size on disk'. The fixed window shows no note (OutcomeNotes collapsed and empty).

On the real user profile (3,332,285 files) the fixed window shows '119 files could not be opened'. Classifying every probe error through the released Core:
- Pre-fix: 119 × 1920 plus 119 × 363 = 238 failures.
- Fixed: 0 × 1920 and 119 × 363.

The 363 files are cloud files whose provider is not running. They stay counted, which is the design's deliberate scope.

I also built a %TEMP% fixture with a socket kept bound, a socket left by raw ws2_32 bind + closesocket, and an alias planted at a 313-character path. Each open with flags 0 gives 1920 and the reparse-point retry gives 0. The pre-fix exe counts them as 'could not be opened'; the fixed exe shows no note.

Other checks:
- Full Core.Tests: 425 of 425 passed.
- Fitness: all 65 rules hold.
- rules-parity: AGREE, exit 0.
- O-002 verified: SL-056's rule 3 only forbids NtOpenFile, so it allows the flag.

Assumption forced by the thin report (title only): the scope is non-link, non-cloud tags, so the 363 cloud files are out of scope. Not reached myself: a real delete race between the two opens, a real 995 cancel, and real ACL denies outside testhost. The shipped --report still cannot show probe failures.

checks.what: Full default Core.Tests suite on HEAD, including ReparsePointProbeTests, ArchitectureRulesTests and RuleCopiesAgreeTests
checks.evidence: Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 425, Skipped: 0, Total: 425, Duration: 21 s

checks.what: Engine fitness check of every declared architecture rule on the working tree (graph rebuilt first)
checks.evidence: 65 rules checked against 118 parsed files (123 read): 'Every declared rule holds.' The new rule 'a refused metadata open is decided in the probe' matches only in 2 comments, which are not counted.

checks.what: O-002: does SL-056's fitness rule 3 allow FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT in SynchronousIoCancel.cs?
checks.evidence: Rule 3 is 'the size probe's open stays on CreateFileW, not a parent-relative NtOpenFile'. It covers files src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/*.cs and must_not_match only NtOpenFile, so it says nothing about the flag. The new OpenReparsePointForAttributes goes through the same private CreateFileW Open, and the Fitness check passes with the flag present at SynchronousIoCancel.cs.

checks.what: Probe-error classification on the real profile through the released Core's own Scanner.Scan and SizeProbe.Probe (reflection, ScanOptions.Probe tap, 8 workers), fixed vs pre-fix (derived C1 and C2, case 9)
checks.evidence: POST: Completed, probes=2,870,414, probeFailures=119, vanished=1. Codes: 363×119 and 2×1; no 1920. PRE: same probes, probeFailures=238. Codes: 1920×119, 363×119, 2×1. All failures are under AppData\Local, and every 363 file carries Archive, ReparsePoint.

No test for cases 9, 10, 11, 12 or 13; the design marked them non-material, 'not worth a test'.

checks.command: the first fixture command, which used Remove-Item Env:… and Remove-Item $log
checks.evidence: Refused before running with 'Remove-Item on system path '*' is blocked'. Re-issued with $env:X=$null and [IO.File]::Delete, and it ran.
Deliberately not re-run: the engine already recorded exit 0 (O-001), and that result is not mine to judge.

The temp folder was deleted: the publishes, Core dlls, hook, pre tree, the socket and long-path alias fixture, and scan logs. git status shows only the engine's own .taad/slices/SL-084 records, as at the start; no tracked source changed.

criteria.criterion: 1. Scan a folder holding an AF_UNIX socket file whose socket stays bound for the whole scan
criteria.how: AnAfUnixSocketBoundForTheWholeScanIsSizedFromItsOwnHandle passed in the 425-test run. Real check: a .NET socket stayed bound in %TEMP% during both published-exe scans; open0=1920, retry=0. Pre-fix it counted toward 'could not be opened'; the fixed window showed no note.

criteria.criterion: 2. Scan a folder holding an app-execution alias (0x8000001B) planted with FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT on a %TEMP% file
criteria.how: AnAppExecutionAliasInAScannedTreeIsSizedFromItsOwnHandle passed. Real check: an alias I planted myself (plant=0, open0=1920, retry=0) was counted by the pre-fix exe and not by the fixed exe.

criteria.criterion: 3. Probe an alias planted on a file holding N bytes
criteria.how: AProbeOfAnAliasOverNBytesReadsTheRetriedHandlesSizes passed (asserts 3 calls and EndOfFile == N). My 3000-byte alias kept its length after the plant, and the fixed exe totalled 3.9 KB with no failure. The listing gives the same figure, so the real run does not by itself prove the size came from the retried handle; the Fact does.

criteria.criterion: 4. Open the planted alias with OpenForAttributes directly (the first, filtered open)
criteria.how: TheFirstOpenOfAnAliasStillFailsAndOnlyTheRetryOpensIt passed. The diff keeps OpenForAttributes at flags 0 (SynchronousIoCancel.cs). My own CreateFileW with flags 0 on real aliases and sockets gave 1920.

criteria.criterion: 5. Probe a plain file with no reparse point
criteria.how: AFileWhoseFirstOpenSucceedsIsNeverRetried passed (plain and WOF files each take exactly 2 calls). plain.bin: open0=0.

criteria.criterion: 6. Scan a plain file refused by a SYNCHRONIZE deny (error 5)
criteria.how: Code contact only. APlainFileRefusedBySynchronizeDenyIsNotRetriedAndStaysProbeFailed passed under testhost: Probe returns 5 after 1 call, and the file stays ProbeFailed and counted. I did not set a real ACL in the published exe.

criteria.criterion: 7. Scan a planted alias with a SYNCHRONIZE deny
criteria.how: Code contact only. AnAliasRefusedBySynchronizeDenyFailsItsRetryAndStaysProbeFailed passed: the first open gives 1920, the retry gives 5, and the file is counted.

criteria.criterion: 8. Probe when the file is deleted between the first open and the retry
criteria.how: Code contact only, through the seam. The ARetryThatFailsReportsItsOwnError Theory rows (2 and 3 not counted as refusals; 5 and 32 counted) passed. No real delete race was attempted.

criteria.criterion: 9. Scan a cloud-tagged file whose provider is not running (363, no RECALL/OFFLINE)
criteria.how: Real check: the fixed Core over the real profile still returns 363 for 119 files (Archive, ReparsePoint), and they stay counted. The fixed window says '119 files could not be opened'. These files are not retried: the retry fires only on == 1920 (SizeProbe.cs). This is the design's deliberate scope.

criteria.criterion: 10. Probe when the first open hangs and is cancelled (995)
criteria.how: Not exercised. Reading the code, the retry is keyed on error == ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE, so a 995 would return unchanged. No test and no run of mine drove a real cancel through Probe.

criteria.criterion: 11. Probe an alias at a path longer than MAX_PATH
criteria.how: Real check through the published single-file exe (the build whose long-path behaviour differs from testhost, per SL-043). An alias at a 313-character path gave open0=1920 and retry=0. The pre-fix exe counted it; the fixed exe did not.

criteria.criterion: 12. Scan an AF_UNIX socket file left on disk after raw ws2_32 bind + closesocket
criteria.how: Real check: dead.sock made by raw socket + bind + closesocket (bind=0, closesocket=0) stayed on disk with ReparsePoint; open0=1920, retry=0. The pre-fix exe counted it; the fixed exe did not.

criteria.criterion: 13. Show the scan's notes in the window when the only reparse-point files are aliases and sockets
criteria.how: Real check: my startup hook read OutcomeNotes in the published exe. WindowsApps pre-fix showed '114 files could not be opened…'; fixed showed Collapsed and empty. The socket and alias fixture showed '2 files…' pre-fix and nothing fixed.

criteria.criterion: 14. Scan the real WindowsApps folder (114 aliases) with the published single-file exe
criteria.how: Real check: the fixed published exe shows 'Finished', 114 files, 26 folders, and no probe note; the pre-fix exe on the same folder notes 114. This was read through the window, not --report, because the schema-1 report carries no probe figure (declared by the builder, confirmed by grep).

obligations.evidence: SL-056's rule 3 (fitness.yaml:704-712, 'the size probe's open stays on CreateFileW, not a parent-relative NtOpenFile') covers src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/*.cs and must_not_match only \bNtOpenFile\b. It does not name FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT or its value, so it allows the flag in SynchronousIoCancel.cs. The retry is the same private CreateFileW Open with the flag added. mcp__taad3__Fitness check (rebuilt) reports all 65 rules holding with the flag present.

not_reached: A real race where a file is deleted between the first open and the retry (case 8). Only the OverrideReparseRetryError seam's simulated errors were exercised.
A real hang and cancel (995) of the first open inside SizeProbe.Probe (case 10). This is argued from code only.
Real ACL denies (SYNCHRONIZE) on plain files and aliases in the published exe (cases 6 and 7). They were only exercised by the xUnit Facts under testhost.

The shipped --report still cannot show ProbeFailures or OutcomeNotes. Case 14 was observed through a validate-only startup hook I wrote, not through any artefact the project ships, so a future regression would not show in --report.

Which reparse tags the other 5 of the profile's 119 pre-fix 1920 failures carried, beyond WindowsApps' 114 aliases. They all disappeared after the fix, but I did not identify them (whether real third-party AF_UNIX sockets exist on this profile is unknown).

A whole-C: scan with the fixed build (only the user profile and WindowsApps were scanned), other volumes (ReFS, removable, network), and a volume without the dedup filter, where review m7 accepts that dedup stubs take the retry.
Windows 10 or any machine other than this Windows 11 26200 PC.

The bug report was only a title. I assumed its scope is non-link, non-cloud reparse tags (sockets and aliases), so the 119 cloud files failing with 363 staying counted is treated as intended, not as a residual bug.
